key_insight: Instead of adding watermarks in image (pixel) space, train compact post-hoc watermarking modules inside the generative model's latent space (DistSeal) to embed detectable signatures with less visual artifact and compute overhead, working across diffusion and autoregressive generators.
problem_solved: Reduces the visual artifacts, computational cost, and model-specific limits of prior pixel-space watermarking by enabling a unified, latent-space watermarking approach that can be applied after model training across different generative architectures.
method: Post-hoc training of small watermarking networks that inject a signature directly into model latent representations rather than final pixels.
Design DistSeal as a unified workflow compatible with both diffusion and autoregressive latent pipelines so the same watermarking procedure transfers across architectures.
Train a detector/verification mechanism that recognizes the embedded latent signature in generated outputs while preserving perceptual fidelity.
impact: Makes provenance and detection of AI-generated images more practical and less intrusive for practitioners, enabling scalable, cross-model watermarking with lower artifact risk and computational cost.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: original latent -> DistSeal watermark module -> generative decoder -> watermarked image; with a parallel detector path.
Side-by-side comparison chart: pixel-space watermarking vs latent-space (metrics: visual quality, compute overhead, robustness, post-hoc compatibility).
Architecture-agnostic icon set showing diffusion and autoregressive models linked to a single DistSeal module to highlight cross-model applicability.
Robustness/attack storyboard: how a detector recovers the watermark under common image transformations (resize, crop, compression).
paper_title: Learning to Watermark in the Latent Space of Generative Models
paper_authors: Sylvestre-Alvise Rebuffi, Tuan Tran, Valeriu Lacatusu, Pierre Fernandez, Tomáš Souček
